about: Each vector holds its input as JSON text (`input`; read it with a parser that keeps a number written with ".", "e" or "E" a float and every other number an integer, as Python's json does), the canonical text solvi gives it (`canonical`) and the SHA-256 of that text's UTF-8 bytes (`sha256`). Kind "value": the canonical JSON of the input. Kind "record": the input is a stored record (a line of a JSONL store); `canonical` is the canonical JSON of its hash body (record_body) and `sha256` its record hash — the `hash` it carries. Kind "chain": `input` is two consecutive stored records; the second one's `prev` is the first one's hash. Floats are written in `input` in another spelling than the canonical one where they can be (1E16, 0.000001, 100.00) so that a port has to reformat them; `source` says which float each was.

vectors.name: float 1e-06 (Python switches to an exponent below 1e-4)
float 1e+16 (Python switches to an exponent from 1e16)
nested objects and arrays, keys sorted at every level
key order: code points, not UTF-16 (astral after U+FFFF)
U+2028 and U+2029 are not escaped
escapes: quote, backslash, controls; / and DEL are not escaped
legacy (records before 0.7): NaN and Infinity tokens
a format 1 record (solvi 0.7.1): the record without id and hash
